title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Assistant Accountant
- Location: Hounslow
- Job Type: Permanent, Full-Time
- Salary: £30,000 to 35k (based on experience)

A returning client of ours is looking for an experienced Assistant Accountant to join a high-quality, multi-award-winning relocation and storage company in London, recognised for excellence in our field. We are looking for an Assistant Accountant to manage both accounts payable and receivable, ensuring efficient financial operations within our dynamic team.

Day-to-Day of the Role:

Accounts Payable:
- Process and input supplier invoices using Dext, Xero, and Approval Max.
- Handle supplier queries, including requests for statements, invoices, and credit notes.
- Check staff expenses and prepare them for payment.
- Conduct monthly supplier reconciliations, addressing any discrepancies and maintaining accurate records.

Accounts Receivable:
- Manage and reconcile various forms of payment receipts including card, SO, Stripe, direct debit, and BACS in Moveware.
- Handle the setup of new storage customer accounts and contract charges.
- Raise storage invoices and credit notes as needed.
- Process and manage customer payments and direct debit mandates.

Credit Control:
- Monitor customer accounts for irregularities and manage credit control processes.
- Send statements and chase overdue payments via phone, email, and letter.
- Handle customer queries and resolve issues promptly.
- File court claims for bad debtors and perform credit checks on new commercial customers.

Additional Duties:
- Prepare reports and perform bank reconciliations between Xero and Barclays.
- Manage administrative tasks, update insurance rates in Moveware, and ensure compliance with payment terms.
- Provide weekly updates to management on storage revenue and turnover.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Proven experience in an accounts office environment.
- Strong bookkeeping skills and experience.
- Proficiency in Xero highly desirable.
- Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to handle multiple tasks.
- Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both internal teams and external clients.

Company Benefits:
- Competitive salary based on experience.
- Structured working hours from 8 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday, with a 1-hour lunch break.
- Opportunity to work in a dynamic, award-winning environment with a strong team focus.

To apply for this Assistant Accountant position, please contact Vinny at the Reed Staines office

title: Client Support Administrator
description:

The firm advises across Pensions, Investments and Life Assurance from the whole of the market and is widely recognised within the industry for the quality of its client service and professional standards.

Due to continued growth, including multiple recent acquisitions across the UK, the business is now looking to appoint two Client Support professionals to join its London team.

The Roles

Two Client Support opportunities are available, offering distinct career paths:

Client Support - FP Administration Pod

This role sits within a team-based support structure and would suit an experienced career Financial Planning Administrator who enjoys a structured environment supporting multiple advisers.

Salary towards the higher end of the banding.

Client Support - Dedicated Adviser Support

This position supports two Financial Planners directly and is well suited to someone looking to broaden their exposure and progress their career within Financial Planning.

Key Responsibilities
- Supporting the financial planning and advice process to ensure a high-quality client experience
- Processing new client documentation in line with internal procedures and data protection requirements
- Creating and maintaining accurate client records on the CRM system
- Liaising with product providers to obtain policy and investment information
- Preparing client meeting packs and supporting documentation
- Working closely with Advisers and Paraplanners to issue reports and new business applications

Candidate Profile

- A methodical approach with the ability to manage and prioritise multiple tasks
- The ability to work well within a team and on their own initiative
- A client-focused mindset with high attention to detail
- IT literacy, including MS Word and Excel
- A desire to pursue or continue financial services qualifications (fully supported)

Package & Benefits
- £32,000 - £38,000 basic salary
- Quarterly bonus (c. 15% of salary)
- Employee Shareholder Scheme
- Comprehensive benefits package
- 25 days holiday plus 3 additional days over Christmas
- Hybrid working - 3 days per week in the office
- Excellent long-term career development opportunities as the firm continues to grow nationally

A first class opportunity to work for a growing business offering genuine career development opportunities.

title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Syntro Partners is working with a growing, PE-backed marketing services group to recruit an Assistant Management Accountant into its London finance team.

This is a strong opportunity for someone who has already built a solid foundation in finance and is now looking for a broader role with more responsibility, more exposure to month-end and management accounts, and genuine scope to develop.

Rather than being confined to one area of finance, you'll work across a busy multi-entity environment, gaining exposure to everything from sales ledger and credit control through to journals, balance sheet reconciliations and management accounts. You'll also be encouraged to look at how systems, technology and automation can improve the way the finance function operates.

The role

Working closely with the wider finance team, you'll take responsibility for a varied mix of transactional and management accounting activity, including:
- Raising sales invoices and managing credit control
- Preparing month-end journals and supporting the production of management accounts
- Supporting balance sheet reconciliations and other month-end processes
- Processing purchase invoices and supplier payments
- Reviewing payment runs before they are released
- Managing employee expenses
- Dealing directly with clients on billing and account queries
- Helping identify opportunities to improve systems, automate processes and reduce manual work

What we're looking for
- You'll ideally have around 2-4 years' experience within an industry finance team and be ready to take the next step in your career.
- You may currently be working as an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, Assistant Accountant or Junior Management Accountant.
- AAT qualified or part-qualified ACCA/CIMA would be useful, but this isn't a role where qualifications or a perfectly matched CV are everything. The bigger priorities are attitude, aptitude and potential.

You'll need to be:
- Bright, curious and keen to understand the wider finance function
- Proactive and comfortable taking ownership rather than waiting to be given every next step
- Confident communicating with colleagues and external clients
- Comfortable with Excel and finance systems
- Tech-savvy, with an interest in how automation and better tools can improve finance processes
- Organised and accurate enough to handle a genuinely varied workload

Why consider it?

The attraction here is breadth and progression.

You'll get exposure across an end-to-end finance function within a growing PE-backed business, rather than spending another couple of years purely focused on transactional accounting.

There's genuine opportunity to take on more as you develop, work closely with experienced finance leadership and build the sort of broad commercial accounting experience that can take you towards a Management Accountant role.

Study support towards AAT or ACCA is also available.

Salary: £35,000 - £40,000 depending on experience

Location: Central London

Working pattern: 4 days per week in the office, 1 day remote

Study support: Available

To apply, please submit your CV for immediate consideration. Due to the volume of applications, we may not be able to respond to every candidate. If you do not hear from us within 14 days, please assume your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Interim Accounts Assistant Creative Agency London (On-site)
description:
Interim Accounts Assistant Creative Production & Events Business London (On-site)

The Client

Harmonic is delighted to be partnering with a well-established creative business that delivers high-quality projects and live brand experiences for a portfolio of well-known consumer brands. They operate at the premium end of their market, where craft and quality matter, and take pride in bespoke, made-to-order work. With the finance team evolving, they are looking for a reliable Accounts Assistant to come in and keep things running smoothly through a busy period.

The Role

Reporting to and working alongside the Management Accountant, this is a hands-on, transactional finance role supporting a small, close-knit team based on-site in South West London. You will take ownership of the day-to-day accounts payable and input work: posting purchase invoices, processing timesheets, and handling company credit card and expense reconciliations, keeping the finance function moving while the team finalises its longer-term structure. It is an immediate-start temporary contract with genuine potential to extend, or to convert to a permanent role, for someone who does a great job. The business runs on Xero.

Key Responsibilities
- Post and process purchase invoices accurately and to deadline.
- Process weekly timesheets and reconcile against records.
- Manage company credit card and staff expense reconciliations.
- Support the wider accounts payable cycle, including payment runs and supplier queries.
- Keep the finance inbox and records tidy and up to date.
- Provide day-to-day support to the Management Accountant and wider finance team.
- Help keep things on track through month-end and busier periods.

Essential Experience
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant, Accounts Payable, or transactional finance role.
- Confident posting and processing invoices, and comfortable with the core AP cycle.
- Reliable and able to hit the ground running with minimal training.
- Strong attention to detail and clear communication.
- Available to start at short notice and to be on-site in South West London 5 days per week.

Desirable Experience
- Experience using Xero (or a similar accounting package; the core skills transfer).
- Exposure to timesheet processing, or to a project-based or creative business.

At Fifosys, we are proud to be ranked among the top 10 Managed Service Providers globally, and we are continuing to grow!

We are now seeking a proactive, detail-driven Credit Control & Accounts Receivable Administrator to join our Finance team and play a key role in maintaining strong cash flow, clean ledgers, and robust financial controls across the business.

If you enjoy taking ownership, working with customers to resolve payment issues, and keeping things accurate, organised, and compliant, this could be a great next step for you.

The role

You will support the effective operation of our Credit Control and Accounts Receivable functions, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and excellent stakeholder communication.

Credit Control
- Proactively chase outstanding customer payments by phone and email
- Liaise with customers to agree payment dates and resolve disputes
- Produce aged debt and bad debt reports for internal stakeholders
- Maintain clear and accurate records of customer interactions
- Support bad debt reviews and escalation processes

Direct Debit Management
- Process Direct Debit collections accurately and on time
- Manage Direct Debit amendments, cancellations, and customer queries
- Reconcile Direct Debit receipts and investigate discrepancies

Accounts Receivable Ledger Management
- Allocate receipts against sales invoices
- Investigate and resolve unallocated cash
- Maintain clean, accurate AR ledgers
- Perform customer account reconciliations where required
- Support the resolution of historic balances and billing discrepancies

Bank & Cash Reconciliations
- Post bank transactions accurately and promptly
- Complete regular bank reconciliations for receipts and payments
- Escalate unreconciled items in line with internal controls and month-end deadlines
- Support month-end close through timely completion of reconciliations

Credit Card & Mailbox Management
- Review and obtain supporting documentation for credit card transactions
- Post and reconcile credit card transactions accurately
- Monitor cardholder spend, approvals, and missing documentation
- Manage shared finance mailboxes, ensuring timely and professional responses

What we are looking for

Experience & Skills
- Experience in Accounts Receivable, Credit Control, or a similar finance role
- Ability to manage the credit control function in a standalone position, reporting into a Senior Finance Manager, within a small team.
- Strong understanding of invoice processing and receipt allocation
- Experience managing customer debt and payment queries
- Good working knowledge of finance systems (Oracle NetSuite desirable) and Excel
- High attention to detail and accuracy
- Ability to manage workload effectively and meet deadlines
- Clear and confident communication skills (written and verbal)

Personal Attributes
- Proactive and solution-focused
- Highly organised with strong time management skills
- Comfortable managing competing priorities
- Professional and resilient when handling customer conversations
- Committed to continuous improvement
- Adaptable in a fast-moving environment

- Competitive salary, aligned to experience
- Company sick pay
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Electric car scheme, supporting sustainable travel choices
- Company pension scheme
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Hybrid or flexible working options
- A strong focus on wellbeing and work-life balance
- Regular social events and team activities help build real connections
- Opportunities to grow and develop within a scaling, acquisitive business

About Fifosys

Founded in 2001, Fifosys delivers premium managed IT services to organisations across a wide range of industries. We've held ISO 27001 certification continuously since 2013 and are recognised as a leading UK MSP through the Channel Futures MSP501 rankings.

Over the last five years, we've achieved strong organic growth, supported by strategic acquisitions with further growth plans ahead. We're proud of our people-first culture and our commitment to quality, accountability, and collaboration.

title: Maintenance Administrator

The successful candidate will play a key role in coordinating property maintenance, supporting tenants and landlords, liaising with contractors and suppliers, carrying out property inspections and ensuring that all properties remain well maintained and compliant with relevant regulations.

Key Responsibilities
- Answer incoming telephone calls and respond professionally to client, tenant and contractor enquiries.
- Manage the maintenance diary and coordinate appointments and property access.

- Coordinate and monitor repairs and maintenance works from initial reporting through to completion.
- Liaise with builders, contractors and suppliers daily.
- Obtain and compare quotations for maintenance and building works.
- Work with landlords to agree quotations and arrange approved works.
- Monitor the progress of contractors and ensure works are completed to an appropriate standard and within agreed timescales.
- Maintain accurate records of all maintenance works, contractor details, quotations, receipts and invoices.
- Carry out regular property inspections, including three- to six-monthly inspections, and prepare detailed reports for property owners.
- Manage the move-in and move-out process, including inventories and relevant tenant documentation.
- Register new tenants for applicable utility services.
- Enter and maintain accurate property, tenant and contractor information within the company's database and specialist property-management software.
- Monitor property compliance, including EPCs, Gas Safety Certificates and Electrical Safety Certificates.
- Monitor HMO and selective licence-related requirements, including fire safety regulations, licences and relevant certificates.
- Maintain accurate records of HMO licence and certificate expiry dates using the company's database system.
- Assist landlords and tenants with general property management queries.
- Work closely with the finance team to ensure contractor invoices are received, processed and paid promptly.
- Follow up on outstanding invoices and documentation where necessary.
- Assist with general office administration and ensure the office filing system is organised and maintained.
- Support the wider team and provide cover for colleagues when required.
- Carry out any other reasonable administrative and property-management duties as required.

Essential Skills & Experience

The successful candidate will be:
- Professional, discreet and confident when dealing with clients, tenants and contractors.
- An excellent communicator with strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Highly organised, reliable and able to manage multiple priorities effectively.
- Comfortable working independently while also contributing positively to a team environment.
- Able to work under pressure, meet deadlines and manage a varied workload.
- Confident dealing with challenging situations and resolving day-to-day issues in a polite, professional and positive manner.
- Trustworthy and able to maintain confidentiality at all times.
- Customer-focused, with a professional and approachable telephone manner.
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail and time-management skills.
- IT literate, with a good working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and standard office systems.
- Comfortable learning and using specialist property-management and database software.
- Flexible and willing to assist with other duties and cover colleagues when required.

Qualifications & Experience
- Previous administration experience is desirable.
- Previous experience within property management, maintenance administration or a similar environment would be advantageous.
- GCSEs and A-Levels, or equivalent relevant qualifications, are required.
- Experience dealing with customers, contractors or suppliers would be beneficial.
- Knowledge of property compliance, HMO, Selective license requirements or maintenance coordination would be an advantage, although training may be provided for the right candidate.
- UK Driving License or Motorbike license

What We Offer

This role provides an excellent opportunity to develop your skills and build a long-term career within a growing property management organisation. You will become an integral part of a friendly and supportive team, with opportunities for career progression as the business continues to expand.

Salary: £12.71.00-£13.00 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications

Working Hours: Monday to Friday, 9.00 am-5:30 pm

Location: London (N8)

Employment Type: Full-time

description:
Continuity of Care Coordinator

Location: Based primarily at HMP Brixton

Salary: £18,049.02 per annum

Vacancy Type: Permanent

About The Role

Are you passionate about improving outcomes for people leaving prison and making sure they receive the right support when they return to the community?

We're looking for an enthusiastic and organised Continuity of Care Coordinator to join our substance misuse team at HMP Brixton. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in strengthening the journey from prison into community treatment, building effective partnerships and helping ensure people leaving custody experience a safe and supported transition.

Based primarily at HMP Brixton, you'll work across our London services, including HMP Wormwood Scrubs and Heathrow IRC, so some travel will be required. Reasonable travel expenses will be covered.

What you will be doing

You'll be at the heart of improving continuity of care across our London prison services. Your responsibilities will include:
- Leading monthly release audits, ensuring service users are correctly discharged on NDTMS and that any data issues are identified and resolved.
- Completing pre-release audits to make sure community teams are fully informed and prepared for an individual's release.
- Ensuring alert forms and key information are shared with community services so that support can continue without unnecessary delays.
- Building strong relationships with local authority and community substance misuse teams, developing effective referral pathways and joint-working arrangements.
- Keeping up to date with local community treatment offers and ensuring prison teams have the information they need to support successful referrals.
- Establishing and chairing continuity of care forums, bringing partners together to identify challenges, share learning and improve outcomes.
- Producing accurate meeting minutes, actions and progress updates, ensuring agreed improvements are followed through.
- Acting as a key point of contact for community prison in-reach workers, helping them overcome barriers and supporting effective pre-release reviews.
- Leading regional NDTMS and other relevant audits, identifying opportunities to improve data quality and performance.
- Supporting the organisation of release fairs and events within the prison, helping service users connect with community support.
- Regularly reviewing and updating the Continuity of Care Best Practice Framework, ensuring it reflects current guidance and good practice.
- Developing strong community partnerships that improve continuity of care and outcomes for service users.
- Working collaboratively with Health and Justice colleagues, NHSE and OHID to support the delivery of commissioning projects and initiatives.
- Sharing best practice, progress and learning with managers and teams across the region.

What we are looking for

We're looking for someone who is passionate about partnership working and committed to making a real difference to people moving from prison back into the community.

You'll ideally bring:
- Experience of working within substance misuse, health, criminal justice or a related setting.
- A strong understanding of the challenges people can face when transitioning from prison into community services.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work confidently with a wide range of partners.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage audits, meetings, actions and deadlines effectively.
- Excellent attention to detail, particularly when working with data, records and performance information.
- The confidence to chair meetings, influence others and drive actions forward.
- Experience of working collaboratively across different organisations and professional teams.
- The ability to identify barriers, find practical solutions and continuously look for ways to improve services.
- A proactive and motivated approach, with the confidence to work independently while also being a strong team player.
- A commitment to person-centred support, equality and improving outcomes for people affected by substance misuse and the criminal justice system.
- The flexibility to travel between London sites when required.

This is more than an administrative coordination role. You'll have the opportunity to shape how continuity of care is delivered across London, strengthen relationships between prison and community services, and help ensure people leaving custody have the support they need to move forward.

If you're passionate about partnership working, improving services and making a meaningful difference to people's lives, we'd love to hear from you. Travel across London may be required.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

title: Network and Funds Coordinator
description:
- Salary - £30,875 - £31,688
- Location - London, United Kingdom
- Team - Network and Funds Directorate
- Line Manager - Director of Network and Funds
- Hours - 35 hours per week
- Contract - Fixed Term (12 months)
- Deadline - 8 October 2026 (23:59 BST)

The Vacancy

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Network and Funds Coordinator plays a key role within Start Network's Network and Funds Directorate, providing trusted, high-quality support to the Director of Network and Funds and helping to keep a busy, strategic portfolio of work moving forward. From coordinating priorities, meetings and communications to building strong relationships and keeping actions on track, the role brings organisation, momentum and attention to detail to the Director's day-to-day work. Working with discretion, initiative and professionalism, the Coordinator will create the structure and connections that enable the Director to focus on strategic priorities and delivering impact. This is a varied and rewarding role for someone who enjoys making things happen, anticipating what is needed and contributing to the smooth and effective running of a dynamic Directorate.

WHAT IS START NETWORK?

Our purpose is to be a catalyst for system-level change that improves the efficiency, effectiveness and ethics of humanitarian action. We do this by working as a network to develop, test & spread new ways of collaborating and resourcing locally-led crisis response and anticipation.

Our current membership is made up of nearly 145 local, national and international NGOs based all around the world. We also support 10 national and regional hubs made up of civil society organisations and NGOs as our vehicle for devolving power, resources and accountability.

OUR VALUES

WE PUT PEOPLE FIRST: Communities come first in our decision-making and programming.

WE ARE BRAVE: We have great ambition and are willing to explore new things and take risks to achieve it

WE OPERATE COLLECTIVELY: We leverage the value of working as a network, sharing risk and resources, and learning together.

WE ARE INCLUSIVE: We see the value in diverse perspectives and work to remove the barriers that prevent voices from being heard.

WE ARE OPEN: We work transparently and with integrity, building mutual trust in all levels of our work, from governance to programming.

WE ARE ETHICAL: We behave and operate based on key principles of anti-racism, non-discrimination, and anti-colonialism. This is a work in progress.

OUR OFFER TO YOU
- Being a part of a network involved in bringing change to the humanitarian sector.
- Hybrid working with options to work from home and remotely to support your work/life balance
- Employee Assistance Programme through Smart Health (depends on the country based)
- Family friendly policies, e.g., flexible working, maternity policy, parental leave and more!
- 25 days' holiday (if UK based) plus 2 company days over the End of Year period for all staff (depends on the country based)

INFORMATION FOR CANDIDATES

Our roles are open to discussion about flexible working. For part-time working and job-shares, please get in touch with us before putting in an application.

We are committed to ensuring that our recruitment process is accessible, inclusive and fair to all candidates. If you require a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the recruitment or selection process, please let us know. We will work with you to understand your needs and, where reasonably practicable, put appropriate adjustments in place to support your full participation.

Start Network is committed to protecting people, particularly children, at-risk adults and affected populations from any harm. We are also committed to safeguarding staff from any forms of bullying, harassment, sexual harassment, discrimination, and abuse of power as outlined in the Dignity at Work policy. Start Network embraces diversity, promotes equality of opportunity and eliminates unlawful discrimination. We are an equal opportunities employer and treat every application on merit alone. We particularly encourage applications from disabled, BAME, LGBTQ+ and non-binary candidates. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for disabled applicants who meet our essential selection criteria set out in the Person Profile.

APPLICATION

Please contact the People and Culture Team if you have any questions or need support with your application.

We use Recruitment+ IRIS Cascade as our online recruitment platform. Recruitment+ IRIS Cascade allows you to demonstrate your skills and abilities through blind-review by our team to reduce bias.

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications and we may review candidates on an ongoing basis, so please apply early where possible to avoid disappointment.

Any offer of employment will be conditional subject to relevant checks. Please refer to our privacy candidate privacy notice regarding treatment of your data. Start Network also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. The core of the scheme is that participating organisations share information about safeguarding-related misconduct (i.e., sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment) that a candidate has been found to have committed during employment, or incidents under investigation when the candidate left employment. For more information regarding this scheme, please visit their website.

The Company

Start Network is made up of more than 90 non-governmental organisations across five continents, ranging from large international organisations to local and national NGOs. Our programmes allow members to deliver humanitarian action around the world.

We are a fast-paced recruitment company specialising in the education, tutoring and social work sectors. Due to the high volume of workers we support, we are looking for an organised, accurate and proactive Payroll Assistant to join our busy payroll team.

This is a hands-on role supporting the processing of payroll for many temporary and contract workers. You will work closely with our recruitment and operations teams, managed service vendors and local authorities to ensure hours are received, checked and processed accurately and on time.

- Process leavers/finishers accurately and ensure all necessary records are updated.

- Investigate discrepancies and resolve payroll issues quickly and professionally.
- Assist with payroll checks and reconciliations before payroll is finalised.
- Ensure all required payroll reports are produced and checked.
- Maintain accurate records and ensure payroll information is kept up to date.
- Work closely with recruitment and operations teams to resolve missing information or discrepancies.
- Assist with ensuring compliance with relevant payroll legislation and processes.
- Support the payroll team with general administration and other payroll-related tasks as required.

Payroll Knowledge

The ideal candidate will have a good working knowledge of, or be keen to develop their understanding of:
- PAYE and income tax
- National Insurance (NI)
- Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)
- Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP)
- Holiday pay
- Starters and leavers
- Payroll deductions
- Timesheet and payroll processes

You don't need to be an expert in every area from day one, but you should have a good understanding of payroll principles and be keen to build your knowledge.

Systems & Skills

Ideally, you will have:
- Experience using Merit Payroll Software or a similar payroll system.
- Experience working with managed service providers/vendors and submitting hours to local authorities.
- Strong Excel and data-entry skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- The ability to work confidently with large volumes of data.
- Good organisational skills and the ability to manage deadlines.
- The ability to prioritise effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive approach to resolving queries.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to work independently while also being a strong team player.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who is accurate, reliable, organised and quick to respond.

Our payroll environment is busy and high-volume, so you will need to be comfortable working to tight deadlines and dealing with a variety of queries throughout the day. Attention to detail is particularly important, as even small errors can have a significant impact on workers' pay.

The right person will also be someone who wants to learn and progress. Initially, you will support the payroll function, but as your knowledge and confidence develop, you will be expected to take increasing responsibility for the payroll process.

Development of the Role

The long-term aim is for the successful candidate to become confident in running payroll independently, including:
- Setting up new bookings and workers correctly.
- Checking and processing hours.
- Ensuring starters and finishers are recorded correctly.
- Carrying out payroll checks and reconciliations.
- Running and reviewing all required payroll reports.
- Dealing with payroll queries and resolving discrepancies.
- Ensuring payroll is processed accurately and on time.
- Taking ownership of the payroll process from start to finish.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a strong payroll administration background who wants to develop their skills and take the next step towards becoming a fully independent payroll professional.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic, reliable and efficient Receptionist who will join the Reception team in acting as the first point of contact for patients, visitors, and healthcare professionals. The role involves providing a welcoming, professional, and efficient service, and a mixture of administrative duties that support the smooth day to day running of Reception. The Receptionists acts as the first point of contact for patients and supports the smooth day to day running of the service by managing enquiries, appointments, and patient requests. The role involves accurate use of clinical systems, maintaining confidentiality, supporting patient navigation and triage processes, and supporting delivery of QOF, enhanced services, and local borough services. The role requires strong communication skills, professionalism, and a patientfocused approach. The following are the main duties and responsibilities of the Receptionist. There may be a requirement to carry out other tasks which will be dependent upon factors such as workload, staffing levels and the needs of the practice: Acting as the first point of contact for patients, carers, visitors, and staff, providing a friendly, professional, and patientfocused service. Handling telephone calls, online requests (via the practices online consultation provider, PATCHS), and facetoface enquiries efficiently, ensuring patients are supported and signposted appropriately. Supporting patient navigation and triage by gathering relevant nonclinical information and following agreed practice guidelines and clinical skill mix. Accurately using NHS clinical systems, e.g. SystmOne, AccuRx, PATCHS, to update patient records, process correspondence from patients and external organisations. Supporting delivery of NHS services including QOF, enhanced services, vaccination programmes, and call recall processes Performing a range of administrative duties including scanning and coding of clinical letters, patient registrations, verifying online requests, monitoring the practices email account, and appropriately booking patient appointments.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: We are looking to recruit a friendly full time and part time GP receptionist/administrator. This will include working morning and evening shifts on rotation. The post requires someone with initiative, enthusiasm, excellent communication skills, empathy with patients and colleagues, well organised, reliable and with a flexible approach to team work. The role involves reception and admin duties both patient facing and over the phone. You will need excellent organisational, communication and interpersonal skills, along with the ability to work as part of a team while managing your own workload The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice, including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the senior receptionist/practice manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Greeting patients Opening up/locking-up of Practice premises and maintaining security Printing blood forms. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non General Medical Services) Picking up calls from patients and other services, e.g hospitals. Assisting doctors and patient with queries. Liaising with hospitals and pharmacy Submitting e-consult lites Processing e-consults and e-consult lites Triaging patients to the appropriate services available. Completing tasks from clinicians Scanning and filling clinical/admin letters. Processing incoming post and emails Forwarding prescriptions to the doctors. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately. Process samples received from patients following urine protocol. Process referrals on a day-to-day basis ensuring they go to the correct service.

title: Receptionist
description: Blackheath Standard PMS are looking for an experienced and reliable receptionist to join our friendly Reception Team. The practice is situated in a pleasant part of Blackheath in South East London with good transport links and local shops. The position is for 22 hours per week over four days, based on a seven week rolling rota. Please note that the rota is variable and you will be working different days over a seven week period. This is based on a 7am start and 12.30pm finish 8am start and 1pm finish, 1pm start and 6pm finish, 1.30pm start with a 7pm finish. This can vary , depending on the needs of the practice during sickness and annual leave. Flexibility is essential. Saturday mornings are part of our enhanced access service and there is the option to work these sessions on a rotation basis. We are a friendly team, who are supportive of each other and there will be opportunity to develop new skills. Duties include: Covering reception desk, answering telephone calls, booking appointments via AccuRx triage system, dealing with patient queries, order prescriptions, process admin duties for clinical staff, general administration such as filing and liaising with other health care providers in a professional manner, and processing clinical letters through the Docman system. The duties are variable, depending on what is required on the day. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn. The applicant must have the ability to prioritise workload. Applicants must have the ability to work within a team, have experience of EMIS, AccuRx and Docman and IT skills. Previous experience of working in General Practice is essential, further training will be available for any candidates that show a passion for learning. Job Description Main duties include: Covering reception desk greeting patients and visitors with a professional and friendly manner. Manage the booking system efficiently, signposting patients to the relevant services. Answering incoming calls, respond to queries and manage email correspondence promptly. Assist clinicians as needed, including handling paperwork, stocking consultation rooms and daily end of day duties to ensure the rooms are meeting infection control standards. Manage office supplies, handling incoming/outgoing post and perform general administrative duties. Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn and develop their skills.In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy. The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues. The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment. The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise needs of people for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.

description: We are looking for a friendly, organised and professional Receptionist/Patient Services Advisor to join our friendly, dedicated team for 16.75 hours per week. This is a vital frontline role that contributes to the smooth running of the surgery and ensures our patients receive a high-quality, welcoming and efficient service. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for patients and visitors and will play an important role in supporting both clinical and administrative functions within the practice. This role requires flexibility to work across our two surgery sites in Purley and Coulsdon, with the ability to provide cover for colleagues during annual leave, sickness and other absences when required. Scan and file clinical correspondence and documents to patient records Provide administrative support to clinicians, management and the wide practice team Ensure patient information is handled confidentially and in accordance with practice policies and data protection requirements.

title: Receptionist
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated and enthusiastic receptionist to join our friendly and supportive team at Gordon House Surgery. We are seeking an individual with excellent customer service skills who enjoys working with people and thrives in a busy environment. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play a vital role in delivering a professional, efficient and compassionate service. The successful applicant will have strong communication skills, a positive attitude, excellent attention to detail and the ability to remain calm when working under pressure. Previous experience in a GP Practice, NHS setting or healthcare environment is desirable. The successful candidate will be responsible for: Providing a courteous and professional reception service to patients and visitors. Managing incoming telephone calls and responding appropriately to patient enquiries. Booking, cancelling and amending appointments in line with practice procedures. Registering new patients and maintaining accurate patient records. Processing correspondence and administrative tasks. Managing patient requests, signposting and directing patients to the appropriate service. Handling confidential information in accordance with GDPR and NHS confidentiality requirements. Supporting clinicians and the wider practice team with administrative duties. Scanning, filing and maintaining accurate electronic records. Contributing to an efficient and patient-focused service The Medical Receptionist role is for an enthusiastic, positive, self-motivated individual who can work both independently and as part of our growing team. Our reception team are the first link for many patients and visitors who come to the surgery. The role varies on a day-to-day basis including greeting patients as they arrive and checking them in, collecting patient notes and ensure that these vital records go to the right healthcare professional. The day-to-day also involves using the clinical system and other software programmes to make appointments, booking patient transport, booking interpreters and dealing with test results. In addition, responding to tasks from clinical and non-clinical staff, liaising with external community services and emergency services and general administration. Our reception team meet regularly to discuss best practice and ways of improving our service; we work very closely with other teams within the practice and community. Desired skills include: - efficiency and ability to multi-task - good communication skills - discretion and respect for confidentiality - a friendly, sympathetic/reassuring manner - great team-working - knowledge and use of Microsoft Office suite - positive, can-do attitude - flexibility From time-to-time we ask our reception team to cover annual leave of other team membersthrough working paid over-time. Being flexible is important to us.

title: Receptionist
description: We require an experienced switchboard operator who has good interpersonal skills and a welcoming personality to be responsible for the reception area. This area is the first point of contact for patients and visitors so a friendly manner and excellent communication skills are essential. The role requires some light administration duties, so the successful applicants must be computer literate, as well as having the ability to be flexible and to act calmly under pressure. To manage and maintain an efficient switchboard and reception service in a professional, friendly and competent manner. To provide an efficient administration and clerical service for the reception area, and other departments when required. To practise good customer care and maintain patient confidentiality at all times To ensure the highest levels of customer care at all times. To ensure all phone calls are dealt with, in a prompt, efficient and courteous manner. To greet all visitors and ensure that all visitors follow the procedure i.e. signing in, wearing a visitors badge, etc and waiting to be announced to who they are visiting. To communicate with the general public, relatives and patients, sometimes dealing with difficult and stressful situations, whilst maintaining tact and confidentiality, at all times. To manage the smooth and efficient administration of the reception area. To ensure that all visitors to the wards or departments are correctly challenged and that the visit is announced and agreed with the relevant area before they leave reception. To be responsible for allocating bleeps to appropriate staff and ensuring bleeps are in working order. To be responsible for booking patient transport as requested, as outlined in the Transport Policy. To assist the clinical staff in moving patient within the reception area i.e. by wheelchair. To assist with the collection of pharmacy/ blood sample/ specimen as requested To ensure all deliveries are signed for, and are promptly collected from reception and to be alert of security measures at all times. To be responsible for receiving all stores and good and distributing to all department. Maintain supplies of appropriate literature in the reception area. To be responsible and accountable for the safe keeping of all keys to units/departments held in reception out of hours. To respond in event of emergency alarm such as fire alarm and panic alarm and ensure is re-set. To participate in the training and development of new bank receptionists, ensuring that they follow guidelines laid down for the reception duties In the event of failure of the telephone system for the hospital, to be responsible to implement the necessary action plans to ensure that an emergency service is provided, until the fault is rectified. To be responsible for keeping the reception area to high standard. To provide an efficient administration and clerical service for the reception area. To provide word processing and administration for other departments (namely Fundraising and the Senior Management Team) as required To assist in providing requested information when audits and organisational surveys are taking place. To receive and sort incoming mail and allocate to appropriate departments To receive and frank all outgoing post ready for post collection. To be responsible for the franking machine and liaise with the Post Office for any changes affecting postal rates. To maintain all relevant directories and filing to enable easy access to information in the reception area. Maintain all receptions filing in such a way that it enables documents to be filed and retrieved in a prompt and efficient manner. To be responsible for the booking of the conference/meeting rooms/boardrooms. Ensure hospital premises are safe by carrying out Site patrols, CCTV monitoring, alarm monitoring and car park management. Complete daily reports of accidents or incidents and ensure the necessary action is taken. Assist in preventing acts of violence, crime or disorder.

title: Administrator/Receptionist
description: Bounds Green Group Practice, a busy and well-establish GP Practice in Haringey, North London, is seeking an enthusiasticMedical Receptionist/Administratorto join our friendly and supportive Medical Administration team. We are a short distance from Bounds Green tube station (Piccadilly line) and Bowes park station (Overground) We have an excellent team of GPs and Nurses, a supportive Management Team and efficient administrative team. Our Practice list size is approximately 19,000 and we are proud to be a part of Haringeys North Central Primary Care Network, working closely with neighbouring Practices. We are open to full time and part time applicants and can offer a range of shifts between Monday to Saturday. Hours of work are negotiable but may involve a combination of early starts (8am) and late finishes (6:30pm). What we offer A competitive salary Paid 30 minute lunch break per day NHS Pension scheme Paid DBS Starting with 20 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) increasing with service Free on-site car parking Supportive and welcoming team environment Full training and development opportunities This is a varied, rewarding position in a busy GP practice setting. The Medical Receptionist/Administrator will work across both administrative and reception functions within the practice, providing reliable operational support to clinicians and the wider multidisciplinary team. The role requires an individual who can work confidently with clinical systems, manage competing priorities, and provide a professional patient-facing service while exercising judgement and initiative. Main duties and responsibilities of the post 1. Administrative and coordination responsibilities Undertake a broad range of administrative duties to support the effective running of the practice Process patient information (electronic and hard copy) accurately, securely, and in a timely manner Monitor, manage, and action incoming emails, electronic tasks, and workflow requests independently Carry out searches, audits, recalls, and administrative reporting as required Type letters, reports, referrals, and associated clinical documentation Respond to administrative requests from clinicians, using judgement to prioritise actions Identify system issues, workflow gaps, or risks and escalate appropriately Report faults to software suppliers and/or IT support and track progress 2. Reception and patient-facing responsibilities Act as a professional and confident point of contact for patients, both face to face and via telephone Respond to patient enquiries using judgement to prioritise urgent, complex, or sensitive matters Support safe navigation of patients to the most appropriate service in line with practice policy Book appointments, recalls, and follow-ups accurately using the computerised appointment system Monitor patient flow and waiting times and escalate concerns appropriately Explain practice procedures, registration processes, and temporary resident arrangements clearly 3. Clinical systems and medical records Assist with the accurate input, updating, and maintenance of patient records on EMIS Clinically code data and correspondence where appropriate Scan, upload, and file patient-related documentation promptly Open, date-stamp, and distribute correspondence, reports, and results to relevant clinicians Arrange retrieval, transfer, and re-filing of medical records as required 4. Communication and telephone systems Receive and make telephone calls in accordance with practice policy, using clear communication and active listening Take accurate messages and ensure timely communication with clinicians and team members Ensure the telephone system is operational at the start of each day and switched to night service at the end of the day 5. Start and end of day procedures Open the premises at the start of the day, deactivate alarms, and prepare the practice to receive patients Secure the premises at the end of the day, ensuring the building is locked and alarms activated Be able to work shifts between 8.00am and 6.30pm as required 6. Professional responsibilities Maintain strict confidentiality at all times Demonstrate the ability to think independently, problem-solve, and manage competing priorities Use initiative, discretion, and common sense when responding to patient and operational issues Communicate effectively with colleagues, clinicians, and external organisationsMaintain a clean, organised, and efficient working environment Communicate and work collaboratively with colleagues at all levels, treating others with professionalism, courtesy, and respect at all times. 7. Additional duties Undertake any other delegated duties appropriate to the role This job description outlines the main duties of the post and may be reviewed and amended in line with service needs. This post is subject to a three-month probationary period, receipt of two satisfactory references, and a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check.

We are seeking a friendly, welcoming and IT-confident Receptionist / Reception Administrator to join our busy GP practice. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for our patients and will play an important role in creating a positive and welcoming experience for everyone who attends or contacts the practice. description: This position is five day a week (Mon to Fri) on site with no remote working. The trust does not offer visa sponsorship for this post. Tyson West 1 is part of Bethlem Royal Hospital. We offer services for men, aged 18-65, who have acute mental illness and require 24 hour hospital care. Acute illnesses start quickly and have distressing symptoms.We provide care for people who live in the London Borough of Croydon.We offer psychiatric assessment, care and treatment in hospital, which helps to reduce the risk to self and others.Our service brings together teams of health and social care professionals, including nurses, psychologists, OTs, social workers and psychiatrists. Your duties will include: Welcoming and assisting patients at reception in a friendly and professional manner. Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries. Supporting patients with appointments and directing them to the most appropriate service or member of the team. Responding to emails and online enquiries, including our online triage system. Processing repeat prescription requests and dealing with prescription-related administrative queries. Undertaking DOCMAN administration, including scanning, coding and filing incoming. Filing and maintaining patient records and ensuring information is processed accurately and promptly. Completing general administrative tasks to support the smooth running of the practice. Liaising with clinical and non-clinical teams. Handling confidential and sensitive information in accordance with practice policies and NHS requirements. RESPONSIBILITIES To provide a friendly, professional and helpful first point of contact for patients and visitors to the Surgery. To deal with patients by telephone, face-to-face, email and through the Practice's online triage system. To undertake a range of reception and administrative duties to support the smooth and effective running of the Practice. To process patient information and administrative work accurately and in accordance with Practice protocols. To maintain patient confidentiality and comply with information governance and data protection requirements. To work collaboratively with both clinical and administrative colleagues. To remain calm, professional, helpful and courteous when dealing with patients, including during challenging or difficult interactions. TASKS TELEPHONE To log in to the Practice telephony system and respond to telephone calls as quickly and effectively as possible. To deal with, transfer or escalate calls as appropriate, following Practice protocols. To accept, record and transmit information accurately using EMIS, online triage system, generic email and other Practice computer systems. To assist patients with queries, requests and access to appropriate services. To provide a professional, calm and courteous service, including when dealing with challenging or difficult telephone interactions. To maintain confidentiality when discussing patient information over the telephone. To log out of the telephony system at the end of each working session. RECEPTION To receive patients and visitors arriving at the Practice in a welcoming, friendly and professional manner. To assist with patient queries and requests or pass messages to the appropriate person. To confidently navigate patient records using EMIS, Docman and other Practice systems in order to assist with patient queries. To make appointments for patients with the appropriate Practice service using EMIS, where required. To assist patients with the Practice's online triage system, including explaining how to access and use the service and directing patients to the appropriate route where required. To handle queries and requests for information or services and ensure that they are dealt with appropriately or transferred to a GP, healthcare professional, member of staff or outside agency in accordance with Practice protocols. To respond appropriately to patient queries received through generic email and other electronic communication channels, ensuring enquiries are dealt with or passed to the appropriate person. To maintain a professional and courteous approach at all times, including when dealing with challenging situations. ADMINISTRATION To undertake general administrative duties required for the smooth running of the Practice. To process repeat prescription requests and deal with prescription-related administrative queries in accordance with Practice protocols. To undertake DOCMAN administration, including receiving, scanning, attaching, coding and filing correspondence accurately into the correct patient's medical record and routing correspondence to the appropriate clinician or team. To process incoming hospital letters, clinic correspondence and other clinical documentation, ensuring that information is accurately recorded and reaches the appropriate clinician or member of the Practice team. To assist with administrative backlogs and other Practice administrative work as required. To accurately enter, update and maintain patient information using EMIS, Docman, online triage system and other Practice systems. To ensure that all patient information is handled securely and confidentially and in accordance with Practice policies, information governance requirements and data protection legislation. GENERAL To assist as required during periods of staff holiday, sickness, increased workload or other operational requirements. To work collaboratively with clinical and administrative colleagues, supporting one another and contributing positively to the wider Practice team. To maintain a professional, respectful, helpful and courteous approach towards patients, colleagues and other healthcare professionals. To remain calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations and seek assistance from an appropriate colleague where necessary. To contribute to the Practice's commitment to providing safe, compassionate and high-quality care to patients. To maintain confidentiality at all times and not disclose patient or Practice information except in accordance with Practice procedures and relevant legislation.

title: Patient Services Advisor/receptionist
description: Are you an experienced Receptionist/Administrative assistant or someone with transferrable skills who is good with people and can balance a varying workload? The Reception teams across Groves Health are the lynchpin of our business and support the Group to provide a first class service to our patients and the wider community. The role:- This is a varied role which will give you the opportunity to have exposure to different parts of Reception/Administration on a rotating basis within a busy GP surgery. Some of your duties will include:- Booking telephone appointments with patients Managing the incoming email inbox and patient requests Responding to patient queries via the Practice website dashboard Greeting patients when they arrive in the Practice and dealing with queries Calling patients on behalf of GP's to book appointments and relay information Managing incoming mail and distributing/scanning accordingly On occasion opening and closing the Practice Working with outside agencies such as Pharmacies and Care homes for patient care Registering new patients Using Practice software such as EMIS, Docman (training provided) and Office products Groves Health is a successful and trusted provider of NHS services across England. Over the past five years, we have grown from a single practice in New Malden to a team of more than 100 people, providing high-quality care to patients and communities across our four sites in New Malden, Richmond, Wimbledon and Hinchley Wood. As Groves Health continues to grow and expand the services we provide, we are looking for an enthusiastic and reliable Receptionist & Administrator to join our team at Groves Vineyard Surgery in Wimbledon . We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people, is well organised and can manage a varied workload in a busy environment. Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare or administrative setting would be beneficial, but we are also keen to hear from candidates with transferable skills and a strong commitment to providing excellent customer service. Our Reception teams play a vital role in the day-to-day running of our practices. As one of the first points of contact for patients, you will help ensure that patients receive a friendly, professional and efficient service. This is a varied role, providing the opportunity to develop your knowledge and experience across different areas of reception and administration within a busy GP surgery. Your duties will include, but are not limited to: Booking and managing telephone appointments for patients. Managing the practice email inbox and responding to patient requests. Responding to patient queries through the practice website and online services. Welcoming patients to the practice and dealing with their queries in a professional and helpful manner. Contacting patients on behalf of GPs and other members of the clinical team to arrange appointments or relay information. Receiving, sorting, scanning and distributing incoming post and correspondence. Registering new patients and ensuring their information is accurately recorded. Liaising with external organisations, including pharmacies, care homes and other healthcare services, where appropriate to support patient care. Using practice and administrative systems, including EMIS, Docman and Microsoft Office . Full training will be provided where required. Supporting colleagues with general administrative duties and contributing to the smooth running of the practice. Assisting with the opening and closing of the practice when required. We are looking for someone who: Has excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Is friendly, approachable and professional. Has a strong commitment to providing excellent patient service. Is organised and able to prioritise competing demands. Can remain calm and professional when working in a busy environment. Has good attention to detail and is confident using computer systems. Is able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Is adaptable and willing to learn new systems and processes. Understands the importance of confidentiality and handling patient information appropriately. Previous experience within a GP practice, NHS or healthcare environment would be advantageous, but is not essential. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing organisation where you will be part of a supportive team and have the opportunity to develop your skills and experience within primary care. If you are enthusiastic, organised and passionate about providing a high-quality service to patients, we would love to hear from you.

To answer general enquiries. To process repeat prescription requests. Process referrals to external agencies such as secondary care using the electronic referral system (ERS) i. Process calling letters are requested j. Process all DNA letters in accordance with current policy k. Action GP2GP tasks l. Read code data on EMIS Web m. Photocopy documentation as required n. File and store records as required o. title: Medical Administrator
description: HAMPSTEAD GROUP PRACTICE (NW3 2QU) Medical Administrator Part-Time Post (25 - 30 hours per week) Hourly rate: £14.80 - £15.50 Working days: Monday - Friday We are seeking a motivated and reliable Administrator to join our busy and friendly team. The successful candidate will provide efficient administrative and secretarial support to the partners and clinical staff, ensuring high standards of service and patient care are maintained. The role involves managing clinical correspondence, processing referrals via the NHS e-Referral Service, and general administrative tasks. You will also process insurance forms, medical reports and medical record requests within agreed timescales, ensuring accurate record keeping and maintaining strict patient confidentiality. The ideal candidate will have excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team managing a varied workload in a fast-paced environment. Previous NHS or primary care experience and knowledge of EMIS are desirable but not essential. This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive team within a well-established practice for a fixed-term maternity cover position. Provide administrative and secretarial support to GPs and clinical staff Preparation of medical correspondence Process patient referrals using the NHS e-Referral Service Manage insurance forms, medical reports and associated payments Process requests for copies of patient medical records Maintain accurate records and ensure documents are scanned into patient files Support cervical screening programme, QOF and flu campaigns Respond to patient and clinician queries relating to referrals and medical administration Provide occasional reception cover when required Manage workflow and coding Manage and action emails. Assist with Lab results. HAMPSTEAD GROUP PRACTICE Title: Medical Administrator Accountable to: Practice Manager Reports to: Practice Manager Liases with: Patients and Users of the Practice Professional Members of the Practice Team Patient Services Team and administrative staff PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THE ROLE To provide efficient and effective administrative and secretarial support to the partners and medical staff of the practice. The role involves coordinating a range of administrative processes and ensuring services are delivered within agreed quality standards and timeframes. KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Secretarial and Administrative Support Provide efficient and effective secretarial support to partners and medical staff to an agreed quality standard and within agreed timeframes. Type all relevant practice correspondence as required, including Fit Notes requiring GP electronic signatures. Type medical reports as required. Record minutes of meetings when required. Provide administrative support such as photocopying, scanning and postal duties. Clinical Correspondence and Referrals Act as a first point of contact for doctors and patients with queries relating to medical matters and referrals. Process patient referrals promptly using the NHS e-Referral Service (eRS). Check the e-Referral Service system daily for rejected referrals and outstanding referral letters. Follow up queries relating to previously typed or submitted referrals. Deal with Advice and Guidance queries and responses. Maintain systems to ensure prompt processing of referrals and correspondence. Be responsible for two-week wait (urgent cancer referral) safety-net checks, ideally conducted weekly. Provide training to staff on the NHS e-Referral Service process when required. Medical Certification and Clinical Administration Send electronic copies of death certificates to Camden Registrars including patient next of kin details. Send cremation forms electronically to funeral directors and ensure copies are scanned into patient records. Process Telederm referrals including taking photographs of skin lesions and uploading them to EMIS records. Provide training to GPs on Telederm processes when required. Insurance Forms, Medical Reports and Claims Ensure that insurance forms, statutory claims forms and medical report requests are processed within 15 working days. Responsibilities include: Maintaining the insurance/claims and medical reports database. Logging all requests daily with the date received. Forwarding forms to the appropriate GP or partner for completion. Monitoring outstanding requests and following up incomplete forms. Ensuring completed documents are scanned and stored in the patients record. Dispatching completed documentation promptly to patients or requesting organisations. Processing income generated from these services and chasing outstanding payments. Distributing income received to salaried doctors where appropriate. Collating partner income and submitting records to the Business Manager and Finance Administrator for payroll processing. Subject Access Requests (Medical Records) Ensure requests for copies of medical records are processed within 28 working days. Logging all requests with the date of receipt. Preparing copies of paper and electronic records. Completing the initial check for third-party information. Passing records to a GP to check for third-party information. Ensuring redacted pages are scanned and appropriately coded in the patient record. Arranging secure transfer of records via recorded delivery, collection or encrypted email. Cervical Screening Administration Provide administrative support for the Cervical Screening Programme in accordance with national protocols. Inputting smear screening data into patient records. Monitoring and chasing outstanding smear results. Sending recall letters to non-responders. Processing Prior Notification Lists via Open Exeter within deadlines. Managing the colposcopy failsafe system. Supporting quarterly cervical screening targets as part of QoF and Enhanced Services. Medical Records Management Process urgent medical record requests and complete the appropriate request forms. Email urgent requests to PCSE and file copies within patient records. Follow up with PCSE if records are delayed. Ensure newly received records are reviewed by a GP and passed for summarisation if required. Document Management Undertake daily scanning of completed medical reports, insurance forms and related correspondence. Ensure scanning is completed in line with the Docman protocol. Additional Duties Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with information governance requirements. Maintain up-to-date contact records for affiliated organisations and services. Provide support to the management team when required. Assist with reception cover during staff shortages. Support practice activities such as the annual Flu Campaign and QOF targets. Undertake relevant training courses with agreement from the Practice Manager. Prepare refreshments for doctors coffee according to the rota. The Practice Manager will allocate duties, or the Business Manager in their absence. Duties may change to meet the operational needs of the practice. This job description is not exhaustive and may be amended by agreement between the Practice Manager and the post holder.

title: Practice Administrator
